time_reached: ~3.5–2.5 billion years ago — the Archean Eon; stromatolites and cyanobacteria dominate; the banded iron formations begin to form as cyanobacteria start releasing oxygen; Earth is a microbial world
last_topic: The Archean World (~3.5–2.5 Bya) — stromatolites as the first visible monuments of life; microbial mats; the emergence of cyanobacteria and oxygenic photosynthesis; banded iron formations as evidence of early oxygen; foreshadowing the Great Oxidation Event
open_threads: The Sagittarius Dwarf Galaxy — another merger still in progress; its tidal debris wraps around the Milky Way in streams
The Andromeda collision — the Milky Way and Andromeda on course to merge ~4 billion years hence
Dark matter halos: still growing via accretion; the Milky Way continues to cannibalize satellite galaxies (Magellanic Clouds)
The supermassive black hole at our centre (Sgr A*) — how it grew, its relationship to galactic evolution
Population II stars in the halo: the living fossils of the early galaxy, still orbiting in their ancient tilted paths
Jupiter's role as cosmic bodyguard — its gravity shields the inner planets from most long-period comets
The Oort Cloud and Kuiper Belt — relics of the protoplanetary disk; source of comets
Earth's Moon — formed from the Theia impact debris; stabilises axial tilt; slowly receding; tidal forces slowing Earth's rotation over geological time
The origin of Earth's water — debate between main accretion phase vs. Late Heavy Bombardment delivery; carbonaceous chondrite isotopic match
The Isua formation (Greenland) — carbon isotope ratios suggestive of life at ~3.8 Bya; contested but compelling
Hydrothermal vents vs. tidal pools — the debate over where life first emerged (covered in Entry #11 but unresolved)
The RNA World — what came before RNA? How did nucleotides form? The pre-RNA world remains murky
LUCA's environment — what was the Last Universal Common Ancestor actually like? Deep-sea thermophile? Early membrane chemistry?
The transition from RNA World to DNA/protein world — how did DNA take over the storage role?
Stromatolites in Shark Bay — the living survivors of the Archean world, still building in hypersaline lagoons
Banded iron formations — the geological record of the ocean 'rusting' as cyanobacteria released O2; key economic iron ore deposits today (Pilbara, Labrador Trough, Minnesota iron range)
coming_up: Entry #13: The Great Oxidation Event (2.4 Bya) — cyanobacteria flood the atmosphere with oxygen; the first mass extinction; banded iron formations; how poison became the breath of life
Entry #14: The rise of the eukaryotic cell — endosymbiosis; mitochondria and chloroplasts as captured bacteria; the invention of the nucleus; the cell that made complexity possible
Entry #15: Snowball Earth (720–635 Mya) — evidence that Earth froze pole-to-pole; volcanic CO2 rescue; the mysterious Ediacaran fauna that emerged after the thaw
